claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase, dendritic BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a lower-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Single-phase HEAs can have insufficient strength at elevated temperature, while precipitation strengthening can improve their high-temperature strength.
Adding a few atomic percent Al to TiVNbTa and applying a controlled heat treatment will trigger formation of an L12 secondary phase.
The resulting L12 precipitates will be nanoscale, coherent, uniformly dispersed, and embedded in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
Stable coherent L12 precipitates can provide high-temperature strength in HEAs.
Nanoscale ordered precipitates can strengthen a BCC HEA at elevated temperature.
Coherent L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing high-temperature dislocation glide.
L12 precipitation will counteract softening of the BCC TiVNbTa phase at 1273 K.
The modified alloy is expected to reach a yield strength of 400–500 MPa at 1273 K, an improvement of approximately 70–170 MPa over the stated baseline.
The precipitation-strengthened alloy may preserve adequate ductility for use as a heat-transfer interlayer.
The intervention is applicable under mechanical loading near 1273 K, strains up to 30%, and the thermal cycling and heat flux encountered between W and CuCrZr.
The heat-treatment regime can be optimized to form and stabilize coherent L12 precipitates while avoiding coarsening and phase instability.
